newsitem.title: INDIA: India to scrap Internet providers' licence fees.
newsitem.headline: India to scrap Internet providers' licence fees.

text.p: India will not charge a licence fee for Internet access providers and will not limit the number of service providers, a senior Department of Telecommunications official said on Monday.

"We have taken a decision to open up Internet access. These are the salient points of the policy, and we will issue the final draft of the policy in a few weeks' time," said the official, who asked not to be named.
He said the government wanted to promote the unbridled spread of the Internet.
Internet access is currently a monopoly of state-run international telecommunications provider Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd (VSNL).
The official said all access providers would need to connect through VSNL's international gateways and lease capacity from it under the new policy.
He said the policy on licence fees and connecting through VSNL's gateways would be reviewed after two years.

India has about 80,000 Internet subscribers at present. VSNL has about 40,000, while the rest are on the Department of Electronics' Education and Research Network (ERNET), which allows access only to educational and non-profit organisations.
Analysts believe monopoly Internet access has restricted its spread due to high costs, poor service and slow connection speeds.
VSNL charges 15,500 rupees ($433) for 500 hours or one year's subscription to the Internet. ($1 = 35.8 rupees)
